proposals.before: Masters of Ceremonies lead civil officials of the fourth rank and below and military officials of the third rank and below out beyond the gate, where they stand in separate formations;
proposals.after: Masters of Ceremonies lead civil officials of the fourth rank and military officials of the third rank and below out beyond the gate, where they stand in separate formations;
proposals.reason: Chinese 文官四品、武官三品以下 does not mark civil officials as 'and below'; the added scope invents a rank range.

proposals.before: The Palace Commissioner calls for the emperor to bow twice and proclaim, "Long live the Emperor!"; the assembled ministers in attendance bow.
proposals.after: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the emperor to bow twice and proclaim, "Long live the Emperor!"; the assembled ministers in attendance bow.
proposals.reason: 宣徽使 is elsewhere rendered Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; 'Palace Commissioner' is an inconsistent mistranslation of the same office.

proposals.before: The empress takes leave of her parents, paternal uncles and aunts, and elder brothers, each bowing four times;
proposals.after: The empress takes leave of her parents, paternal uncles and aunts, and elder brothers, bowing four times to each;
proposals.reason: Chinese 各四拜 means the empress bows four times to each relative; the literal wrongly makes the relatives the ones bowing.

proposals.before: She is borne with a silver pitcher on her back, silk bands in hand, and walks the yellow path.
proposals.after: Bearing a silver pitcher on her back and silk bands in her hands, she walks the yellow path.
proposals.reason: 負 means she herself carries the pitcher on her back; “is borne” invents a passive carrying that the Chinese does not state.

proposals.before: The empress's elder and younger sisters or younger sisters, and those who accompanied her in bowing, each receive gifts.
proposals.after: The empress's elder or younger sisters, and those who accompanied her in bowing, each receive gifts.
proposals.reason: 後姊若妹 uses 若 as “or”; the literal’s “elder and younger sisters or younger sisters” duplicates 妹 and obscures the meaning.

proposals.before: they bow once more, advance slightly, and submit on behalf the words of those who escorted the empress;
proposals.after: they bow once more, advance slightly, and submit on their behalf the words of those who escorted the empress;
proposals.reason: English “submit on behalf the words” is ungrammatical; the Chinese 附奏送後之詞 needs a possessive “their” after “on behalf”.

proposals.before: they bow once more, advance slightly, and submit on behalf the words of those who escorted the empress;
proposals.after: they bow once more, advance slightly, and submit on their behalf the words of those who escorted the empress;
proposals.reason: Same grammatical failure as the idiomatic field: “on behalf the words” must be “on their behalf the words”.

decisions.reason: s0003 Chinese 〈（嘉儀上）〉 is rendered with English parentheses; the trailing book-title closer 〉 in the idiomatic field is stray markup with no English opener, and removing it leaves an accurate section title.
Same stray 〉 appears in the literal field for 〈（嘉儀上）〉; stripping the unmatched closer yields the correct English section title without inventing or omitting meaning.

In the bureaucratic formula 文官四品、武官三品以下, 以下 marks the shared rank cutoffs—civil officials of the fourth rank and below, military of the third and below—so the original idiomatic scope is accurate; dropping civil “and below” wrongly limits the group to exact fourth-rank civil officials.

decisions.reason: s0120 has 宣徽使, already rendered “Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat” in adjacent s0118 and in this unit’s literal; “Palace Commissioner” is an inconsistent, vaguer mistranslation of the same office, and the proposed title restores consistency without changing the action.

後辭父母、伯叔父母、兄，各四拜 has the empress as subject taking leave, with 各四拜 meaning she bows four times to each relative; “each bowing four times” wrongly makes the relatives the agents, and the proposed wording matches the Chinese and the idiomatic field.

decisions.reason: 負銀罌，捧縢，履黃道行 uses active 負 “bear on the back” and 捧 “hold”; “is borne with” invents a passive carrying absent from the Chinese, and the proposed active wording restores the correct agent.

後姊若妹 uses 若 as “or” (elder or younger sisters); the literal’s “elder and younger sisters or younger sisters” duplicates 妹 and garbles the connective, and “elder or younger sisters” is the accurate fix.
